surfaces.part: bare earth ground patch with scattered weed tufts and two rosettes, seen from above

answer.evidence: The image is a 64x48 fully opaque tile of mottled brown earth with small green weed tufts and two rosettes scattered on it. Every row has width 64, so there is no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no vertical south face. The column scans show only mottled earth tones with occasional green or grey specks, with no band structure. It is a flat ground decal seen from above, which matches the flat kind. There is no front face, so it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown soil ground with small green weed tufts and two rosettes. Measured: 5 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 3%, so there are no big flat areas. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted dark brown or green rather than black. The soil shows grain dots and a few lighter specks, and the tufts have 2-3 greens with darker shadow tones. Shading is a bit shallow, about 4 steps on the soil and 3 on the leaves, against 5-6 in Beodeul. The weeds are sparse and small, so the soil between them is mostly one mid-brown with light speckle. Some texture dots are present but sparse, and the tufts are small and low in contrast. Overall it is slightly thinner than the references but acceptable: tinted outlines, no flat fills, and tone count at or above the grass reference.
